values: Materials and setup｜all fictional data

Fictional P-12 drainage pipeline drawing: A1 specifies a 3.00 meter pipe section with a starting invert elevation of 10.00 meters and an ending elevation of 9.94 meters. Only compute the problem's elevation difference and slope ratio, and do not judge whether it meets real engineering design.
A2 pre-shift record: the underground cable position column is unconfirmed; the trench protection review column is blank, and standing water is found after rain.
A3 project agreement: when any of these three items is unconfirmed, pause trench entry and pipe lowering and hand the decision to the qualified site supervisor.
Tasks and deliverables
Compute the elevation difference and slope ratio for A1 and state the units, calculation, and applicable conditions.
Prepare the A2/A3 start condition form and stop handover note: list the unconfirmed items, material numbers, recipients, and pending decisions.
Reference answer (do it independently first)
The A1 elevation difference is 10.00 − 9.94 = 0.06 meters; 0.06 ÷ 3.00 = 0.02, which is 2%. This is a fictional drawing geometry calculation and does not represent an applicable engineering slope.

The underground utilities, trench protection, and standing water handling in A2 are all unconfirmed; per A3, do not enter and do not lower the pipe section, hand it to the qualified responsible person for verification, and do not set safety thresholds on your own.
Boundaries and scoring

Four-point scoring: the elevation difference is correct, the slope ratio and units are correct, all three unconfirmed risks are listed, and stopping and escalation are clear without impersonating engineering acceptance; one point for each.；Only paper materials are used; do not go to a real trench or touch lifting or underground utilities. A perfect paper score does not prove construction qualification.

title.text: Pipelayer career guide: trenches, pipe connection, wages, and entry paths

subject.name: Pipelayers
subject.summary: Pipelayers lay pipe sections in trenches or in drainage and municipal water supply projects, verify the trench subgrade elevation, pipe position, and joint sealing, and backfill according to the construction plan. Real trench, lifting, and underground utility work must follow on-site safety rules; paper exercises do not constitute operating authorization.
